claims.claim: phi-1, a 1.3B code model trained on filtered web 'textbook quality' data plus GPT-3.5 synthetic textbooks and exercises
claims.quote: phi-1 is a Transformer-based model with 1.3B parameters, trained for 4 days on

claims.claim: Despite small scale, phi-1 reaches 50.6% HumanEval and 55.5% MBPP pass@1
claims.quote: Despite this small scale, phi-1 attains pass@1 accuracy 50.6% on HumanEval and 55.5% on MBPP.

claims.claim: Finetuning on CodeExercises unlocks emergent capabilities absent in phi-1-base
claims.quote: It also displays surprising emergent properties compared to phi-1-base, our model before our finetuning stage on a dataset of coding exercises

claims.claim: High-quality data breaks existing scaling laws; data selection is key to the result
claims.quote: we discuss evidence for the importance of our data selection process in achieving this result

claims.claim: Number of parameters plays a key role in emergence (phi-1 vs phi-1-small)
claims.quote: we confirm the hypothesis that the number of parameters plays a key role in emergence

claims.claim: Alternative evaluation (LLM-graded unconventional problems) and contamination study via data pruning
claims.quote: Finally in Section 4 we discuss alternative benchmarks to evaluate the model and in Section 5 we study possible contamination of our training data with respect to HumanEval.

rerun.quote: See Table 2 for our results with phi-1 and competing models.

scores_copied.quote: We use self-reported scores whenever available.

data_disclosure.quote: A filtered code-language dataset, which is a subset of The Stack and StackOverflow, obtained by using a language model-based classifier (consisting of about 6B tokens).

tokens_disclosed.quote: this is equivalent to ∼ 8 epochs on our CodeTextbook dataset for a total of little over 50B total training tokens.

compute_disclosed.quote: We train on 8 Nvidia-A100 GPUs using deepspeed. Our pretrained base model phi-1-base was obtained in under 4 days of training.

coding.note: No ARCH or TRAIN claims: the paper says its architecture and training are conventional, so ablation is NA throughout. The main table (Table 1) uses self-reported comparator scores 'whenever available', so scores_copied is YES. Rerun is MIXED because the authors ran the comparators themselves on the new Table 2 evaluation. Comparators are capped at 15; CodeGen2-1B, StarCoder-Prompted, CodeT5+ and InstructCodeT5+ were left out. Data disclosure is PARTIAL because synthetic data generation details are withheld 'for proprietary reasons'. A filtering-vs-unfiltered comparison exists for data (350M), but data claims are not coded for ablation. No seeds or variance are reported.
